recommendation.verdict: Cancel all rail subscriptions to save €198 per year
recommendation.summaryText: Annual cost drops to €951.64 (no subscription fees, trips €951.64), saving €198 / year versus your current BahnCard 50. Travel time stays the same, while CO₂ rises by a negligible +0.003 kg / year.
reasoning: Cost advantage: eliminating the €243.96 BahnCard 50 fee and its €45.90 discount reduces yearly spend by €198 with unchanged travel time.
Trade‑off across dimensions: cheaper and equally fast, with only a marginal CO₂ increase (+0.003 kg / year), making the overall benefit clear.
Break‑even insight: with no subscription fees the portfolio’s net subscription cost is €0, so it trivially breaks even.
Continuity: this is the third review flagging the BahnCard 50; earlier you kept it, but the optimizer now again recommends cancelling it.
assumptions: Rail fares are based on historical price classes (Sparpreis/Flexpreis) per route.
Trip frequencies are extrapolated from past travel data and calendar events.
No other personal travel changes are assumed.

A subscription changes what each transport mode costs you; projected mode usage shifts in response (a gradual mode-share shift, not a hard switch), and travel time and CO2 follow. For this persona, time is valued at €3.56/hour and CO2 at €0.111/kg when weighing mode choice, derived from their stated cost/time/sustainability priorities.
